entrypoints.summary: The administration page accepts a multipart POST with attacker-controlled name and magician file fields, and moves the upload to a destination constructed from name.
The rebuild page accepts the GET page parameter, reads the corresponding local file, JSON-decodes it, and interprets its sections.

affected_components.role: Constructs upload path from an attacker-controlled name and stores accepted upload data.
Loads selected page data and dereferences link-section values as local filesystem paths.

code_slices.surrounding_context: The handler checks file -b output for an image pattern and rejects upload paths containing php, while rebuild strips backslashes and applies an unanchored regex before JSON decoding.
code_slices.vulnerable: The upload handler builds $uploadFile from ./magicians/, submitted name, and .magic; rebuild loads ./$pageName; interpret() reads a link section's value with file_get_contents.

capabilities.concept: Placement of upload outside the intended magicians directory

mitigations.concept: Allowlisted canonical filesystem resolution for page and link resources

relation_candidates.dst: Placement of upload outside the intended magicians directory
relation_candidates.rationale: The upload destination is derived by concatenating the submitted name without directory-containment validation.
relation_candidates.src: Attacker-controlled multipart upload name and content

relation_candidates.rationale: The selector is used to read a page file after only an unanchored regex check, and interpreted link values are then passed directly to file_get_contents.

This forms a conditional chain because the rebuild handler reads selected local page data and interprets decoded link values as direct file-read paths; successful upload-content decoding is not demonstrated.
relation_candidates.src: Placement of upload outside the intended magicians directory

relation_candidates.rationale: The interpreter embeds bytes returned by file_get_contents for link sections, and the runtime places a secret at /flag.txt.

relation_candidates.dst: Allowlisted canonical filesystem resolution for page and link resources
relation_candidates.rationale: Mapping identifiers to fixed resources and enforcing canonical containment prevents direct attacker-selected paths from reaching the read operation.

sources.concept: Attacker-controlled multipart upload name and content

impact.affected_asset: Local files readable by the PHP/Apache process, including the challenge secret placed at /flag.txt by the image build.
impact.attacker_capability: Subject to the unverified ability to supply an upload that both passes the image check and decodes into the required section object, an unauthenticated HTTP client can direct the interpreter's link read to a chosen local path.
impact.security_effect: Conditional disclosure of local file contents through rendered rebuild output.

causal_trace.summary: The upload handler constructs its destination by concatenating ./magicians/, the submitted name, and .magic; it does not reject path separators, although it rejects names containing php.

A supplied page value is accepted when it contains a word-character filename substring matching the regex; the match is not anchored and no canonical-path containment check is performed before reading ./$pageName.

For a decoded section whose type is link, the interpreter passes section.value directly to file_get_contents and returns the resulting bytes inside generated markup, without an allowlist or containment check on that value.

The runtime image copies the challenge secret to /flag.txt; if an attacker can cause an uploaded file to be accepted, decoded as a link section, and selected by rebuild, the direct link read can disclose a local file such as that secret in the HTTP response.

failure.operation: file_get_contents($section->value) in interpretation of a link section

primary_invariant.statement: Page definitions and link targets interpreted by the rebuild endpoint must resolve only to server-authorized resources, rather than attacker-selected filesystem paths.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The upload destination incorporates an unnormalized submitted name, the page selector has only an unanchored filename-substring check, and link values reach file_get_contents without path authorization.

quality.review_notes: Primary PHP and runtime artifacts establish the unsafe path construction and direct local-file read. No request/response trace, accepted polyglot payload, execution result, or authored remediation is supplied. In particular, feasibility of one uploaded body passing file -b image classification while surviving normalization and decoding as the required JSON object is not established.

remediation.invariant_restored: Resolve page identifiers through a fixed server-side map, and restrict link resources to a canonicalized, allowlisted directory before any file read; do not let uploaded names determine page-definition paths.

target.component: administration upload handler and rebuild page interpreter
